status_vocabulary.bounded: The current consumer preserves this meaning inside an explicitly narrower claim ceiling.
status_vocabulary.partial: Some structure exists, but one or more required semantic, generated-code, runtime, or evidence surfaces are missing.
status_vocabulary.absent: No current first-class consumer was found in the selected source set.
status_vocabulary.conflict: A current consumer uses the same area or name with semantics that collapse a required distinction.

rows.finding: The responsibility-specific contract is validated and rendered as a named TypeScript type, Python Protocol, or Rust trait; provider runtime remains outside the claim.
Formation is validated and embedded in the manifest, but logical-to-physical mappings are opaque references and no provider adapter is generated.
The local transaction tuple and references are validated, but generated executable unit-of-work seams and runtime guarantee observations are absent.
Outcome classification is represented, but messaging and API-specific mappings are not consistently projected through it.
The durable binding tuple is validated, while the profile explicitly reports provider runtime and durable dispatch as unimplemented.
Concern-specific binding records exist, but there is no common discriminated integration-binding envelope connecting persistence, messaging, and APIs.
A provider-neutral system profile and one AWS recipe selection exist; neither is a reusable provider capability/configuration profile.
Adapter and resource references are accepted as opaque strings, without a typed realization, credential, deployment, or evidence envelope.
Messaging accepts one fixed envelope identifier; versioned schema and compatibility behavior are not first-class.
CLI receipts and observation records exist, but no integration-bound receipt contract connects observed outcomes to a precise claim ceiling.
D46 carries logical_physical_mapping_ref only; entities, values, sums, collections, keys, relations, indexes, and conversions are not structurally mapped.
The selected binding-set schema has no migration contract or compatibility transition surface.
The current transport binding points directly to event_ref, so domain Event and transport Message are not represented as separate nodes connected by a mapper.
One fixed envelope profile is accepted, but envelope fields, versioning, trace context, and compatibility are not typed.
MessageChannel currently uses purpose delivery/dead-letter rather than a discriminated queue/topic/stream/dead-letter semantic kind.
No competing-consumer queue semantic exists.
No fan-out topic with independent subscription state exists.
No retained-log, cursor, replay, or ordering-scope stream semantic exists.
A dead-letter purpose exists, but failure metadata, retention, redrive governance, and source-channel identity are distributed or missing.
TransportBinding combines publication and subscription concerns and omits an Event-to-Message mapper.
Consumer operation references exist on channels, but there is no subscription identity, mapper, completion boundary, or independent policy bundle.
Only at-least-once with bounded receipt fields is accepted; at-most-once is absent and the producer/consumer boundary is not explicit.
provider-accepted is fixed inside delivery policy, conflating producer acceptance with the separate consumer acknowledgement/completion boundary.
Only ordering_scope none is accepted; unordered, key-ordered, and global claims are not modeled as a policy.
The owner is fixed to consumer inbox message ID; key expression, retention, transaction relationship, and duplicate outcome are not first-class.
The current policy combines classification with retry eligibility and terminal dead-letter continuation, crossing the D48 separation boundary.
The composition experiment supports POST node-http and rust-http endpoints, but only inside a separate profile and without a shared integration binding contract.
Dependency contracts and composition integrations can express fragments of a remote capability, but no external-api specialization binds stable typed failures.
provided, http-get, provided-or-http, module-local, and module-http transports exist, but request/response mappers, provider operations, and shared failure binding are not composed.
No sender verification, replay protection, external event identity, or webhook acknowledgement contract exists.
authEnv and secretEnv names exist, but scheme, credential slots, provider, rotation posture, and disclosure boundary are not typed.
Timeout and maximum response bytes exist; retry safety, idempotency, backoff, concurrency, and circuit behavior do not.
No structural mapping from protocol/provider failures to the D48 contract failure surface exists.
ORODI operational observations and CLI receipts exist, but integration stage, binding reference, outcome, sanitized attributes, and claim ceiling are not unified.
The recovery/ORODI work proves bounded local observation and evaluation surfaces, but the generic integration-to-ORODI one-way binding is not part of the system-integration compiler.

System integration generates under src/domainspec/system-integration while reconciled project output has language-specific coherent layout rules; node-scoped generation explicitly rejects the overlay.

work_packages.title: Ontology scaffold and definition traceability
work_packages.outcome: Represent all 36 concepts, their specialization edges, and 15 non-collapse laws as non-authoritative agent-facing navigation records with source-byte closure.

work_packages.title: Shared integration contract kernel
work_packages.outcome: Create the discriminated IntegrationBinding, ProviderProfile, ProviderRealization, SerializationProfile, RuntimeReceipt, and D48-preserving shared contracts.

work_packages.title: Persistence composition
work_packages.outcome: Add typed logical-to-physical mapping and migration contracts while preserving D46 and D47 local-boundary semantics.

work_packages.title: Messaging composition
work_packages.outcome: Separate Event from Message; distinguish queue, topic, stream, and dead-letter; split publication from subscription; and make delivery, acknowledgement, ordering, deduplication, and failure policies orthogonal.

work_packages.title: External API composition
work_packages.outcome: Unify inbound endpoints, outbound API contracts/bindings, webhooks, authentication, resilience, and D48 failure mappings.

work_packages.title: Receipts and one-way ORODI observation
work_packages.outcome: Emit bounded integration receipts and disclosure-safe observations through a one-way ORODI adapter with no control return edge.

work_packages.title: Three-language generation and coherent layout
work_packages.outcome: Generate semantically equivalent TypeScript, Python, and Rust contracts/adapters into the reconciled project layout with closed imports and no generic runtime dumping ground.

work_packages.title: Cross-language product tests
work_packages.outcome: Run positive, hostile, non-collapse, semantic-equivalence, deterministic-output, and native compile tests for all selected integration families.

work_packages.title: Exact product candidate
work_packages.outcome: Freeze one exact candidate and current product-test evidence for review; make no authority request.

work_packages.title: Provider test services
work_packages.outcome: Prepare disposable PostgreSQL, message-broker, and HTTP fixtures only when required by the selected product-test slice.

work_packages.title: Packaging and release integration
work_packages.outcome: Prepare package/release changes only after the exact product candidate is tested and reviewed.

settled_constraints: The language denominator is TypeScript, Python, and Rust; Kotlin is not included.
Integration concepts are contracts and bindings, not new domain meta-types unless a later definition decision explicitly says otherwise.
Provider profiles may refine mechanics but may not redefine domain meaning.
Queue, topic, stream, and dead-letter semantics remain distinct.
Event-to-Message and protocol-to-application conversion use declared Mapping nodes.
D48 failure classification remains separate from retry, compensation, dead-letter, and workflow continuation.
ORODI integration is observation-only and one-way.
No provider selection, runtime guarantee, publication, release, deployment, or production claim follows from this plan.
claim_ceiling: Current-source reconciliation and candidate construction sequence only; not an admitted plan and not implementation authority.
